summary.short: Brazil's Digital Statute for Children and Adolescents (Lei 15.211/2025) requires providers of digital products or services directed at or likely accessed by minors to protect them through safety, age-assurance, parental supervision, content, advertising and reporting duties, enforced by an autonomous authority, effective 17 March 2026 per Art. 41-A.
summary.long: Lei nº 15.211/2025 (Estatuto Digital da Criança e do Adolescente) sets child-protection duties for information technology products and services directed to children and adolescents or likely to be accessed by them, wherever the provider is located (Art. 1). Chapters I and II set principles and general duties: priority protection and best interests (Art. 3), safety and privacy by design with protective default settings (Arts. 6-7), risk management and age-appropriate content (Art. 8). Chapters III and IV bar access to improper content and require age verification without self-declaration (Art. 9), with duties for app stores and operating systems to provide age signals and parental consent for app downloads (Art. 12). Chapters V to VII cover parental supervision tools and default settings (Arts. 16-18), child-monitoring products (Art. 19) and a ban on loot boxes in child-directed games (Art. 20). Chapters VIII and IX ban profiling-based advertising to children (Arts. 22, 26), require guardian-linked accounts for users up to 16 (Art. 24) and set social-network duties. Chapters X to XII cover removal and reporting of child-abuse content, notice-and-takedown and semi-annual transparency reports (Arts. 27-31). Chapter XIII addresses abusive use of reporting tools (Arts. 32-33). Chapter XIV assigns duties to an autonomous administrative authority (Art. 34). Chapter XV sets penalties: warning, per-user or turnover-based fines, suspension and prohibition, applied by the authority or the courts (Art. 35). Art. 39 modulates obligations by service features, reach and size. Art. 40 requires a legal representative in Brazil. Art. 41-A sets entry into force on 17 March 2026.

notes: Consolidated text with amendment marks in brackets.
